correctness.rationale: For a full spanning edge, the successful pure state is \(|a\rangle+\kappa|v\rangle\), where \(\kappa=(e^{i\theta}-1)2^{-n/2}\). On every bipartition of sizes \(k\) and \(n-k\), the two local product rays are independent and the orthonormalized \(2\otimes2\) coefficient matrix has \(\det H=H_{11}=\kappa\sqrt{1-2^{-k}}\sqrt{1-2^{-(n-k)}}\). The partial-transpose determinant is \(\det[(\rho^{T_B})_{4\times4}]=-p^3|\kappa|^4(1-2^{-k})^2(1-2^{-(n-k)})^2\); the formula follows by a rank-one determinant expansion and the pure-state partial-transpose cofactor. For the PPT-mixture statement, a positive-operator decomposition must preserve the rank-two support. The only product rays in that support on every cut are \(|a\rangle\) and \(|v\rangle\). The two-qubit PPT equivalence forces any putative PPT mixture to be diagonal in their two projectors, contradicting nonzero \(p\kappa\) coherence. The boundary cases \(p=1\), \(p=0\), trivial phase and nonspanning edge are proved separately. Finite numerical checks corroborate but do not prove the all-size result.

originality.rationale: The source introduces perfect-or-absent hyperedge randomization and uses finite-size negativity and PPT-mixer numerics, but no exact single-edge all-n classification. The older Chen--Đoković Lemma 12 directly covers qualitative bipartite NPT, which is not claimed as a novel theorem. The accepted novel content is the exact cut determinant for continuous phases and the global PPT-mixture if-and-only-if boundary. The inspected primary sources contain no stronger covering theorem, while generic rank-two consequences are explicitly distinguished.
residual_risks: A differently indexed result could specialize generic low-rank PPT-mixture geometry to this exact randomized hyperedge; no such explicit implication was located.
The qualitative assertion that all splits are NPT already follows from arXiv:1301.2372v1 Lemma 12, so originality must rest on PPT-mixture exclusion and the determinant identity.
The ideal-or-absent single-gate model is narrower than physically realistic circuit noise; no broader robustness is claimed.

value.rationale: The source relies on finite-size PPT-mixture SDPs to characterize noisy hypergraph-state generation. For the natural one-edge baseline, this theorem settles that relaxed multipartite-entanglement decision for every n, all gate-success probabilities, and any phase, and supplies an explicit bipartition spectral certificate. The zero-success-threshold classification is a meaningful boundary separating topology-driven entanglement from the sudden-death behavior of more elaborate randomized hypergraphs. A completely equivalent finite table would not supply the all-size condition; no claim is made about arbitrary multi-edge architectures or experimental noise.
